fixes.explanation: Oil on the head sounds fancy, friend, like a spa day under the oaks. But Abraham keeps it simple. He says, “Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.” (Genesis 18:4). Tired feet and some shade. That's the whole offer.

Robes! Abraham is running a tent, not a department store, friend. His offer is simple: “Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.” (Genesis 18:4). I think a cool wash and some shade were all those travelers needed in the heat of the day.

Honey! Okay, I see you, baker. You're thinking like somebody who has stood in front of a cooling rack. But Abraham says, “And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves.” (Genesis 18:5). Plain bread, and he even calls it a bit. Hold on to that word, because he's about to get carried away in the best way.

A goat is a good guess, friend, but look where Abraham runs. He runs to the herd, and the herd means cattle. There he selects a tender and choice calf (Genesis 18:7). A man who promised a bit of bread is now picking out a whole calf. I think his guests are about to get way more than they ordered.
